messages.content: Use web search to find relevant datasets. Only include landing pages or DOIs. Do not invent links. Do not call time, date, timestamp, or clock tools.

Query: Can you find datasets about Media, POLITICS, Political behaviour and attitudes, and Government, political systems and organisations in Germany during the 2010s?
Respond ONLY as JSON in this exact shape: {"items":[{"title":"...","url_or_doi":"...","justification":"..."}]}. Put any DOI, URL, landing page, or link in url_or_doi.

queries: GESIS German Longitudinal Election Study GLES 2013 2017 dataset DOI
Germany media politics dataset 2010s German media analysis election campaign GESIS
Manifesto Project dataset Germany 2010s political parties DOI
action.query: GESIS German Longitudinal Election Study GLES 2013 2017 dataset DOI

content.text: {"items":[{"title":"German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES) – Federal Elections 2013 and 2017","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/gles/data-and-documentation","justification":"A comprehensive collection of German election datasets covering voting behaviour, political attitudes, party identification, political participation, campaign communication, and media influence. Includes surveys conducted around the 2013 and 2017 federal elections. Particularly relevant for studying relationships between media consumption, political preferences, and electoral behaviour in Germany during the 2010s."},{"title":"German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES) – Media Content Analyses 2013 and 2017","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/gles/overview","justification":"The GLES programme includes media content analyses of German federal election campaigns, examining television news and newspaper coverage of political parties, candidates, and election issues. The 2013 and 2017 datasets are particularly useful for investigating political communication, media framing, campaign coverage, and the relationship between news media and democratic elections."},{"title":"Social Media Monitoring of the German Federal Election Campaign 2017","url_or_doi":"https://access.gesis.org/dbk/63762?download_purpose=-99","justification":"Dataset documenting political communication on social media during Germany's 2017 federal election campaign. Relevant for analysing online campaigning, political parties' social media activities, digital political communication, and public engagement with electoral politics. Provides empirical material for studying the growing importance of social media in German politics during the 2010s."},{"title":"Political Campaigning on Twitter During the 2019 European Parliament Election Campaign","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/elections/web-data","justification":"GESIS provides social media research data covering political campaigning on Twitter during the 2019 European Parliament elections. Relevant for studying German political actors' digital communication, online political engagement, party messaging, and the use of social media in European electoral politics. The dataset enables investigation of political communication at the end of the 2010s."},{"title":"ALLBUS – German General Social Survey, 2010–2018","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/allbus/data-and-documentation","justification":"A major representative population survey programme covering German society throughout the 2010s. Survey waves from 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, and 2018 provide information on political attitudes, institutional trust, political participation, democratic values, and social characteristics. Particularly useful for examining changes in political culture and public opinion across Germany over the decade."},{"title":"Politbarometer – German Political Opinion Surveys, 2010–2019","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/elections/politbarometer","justification":"A long-running series of representative German public opinion surveys measuring attitudes toward political parties, politicians, government performance, and current political issues. Monthly surveys throughout the 2010s make this resource particularly valuable for tracking political preferences, electoral intentions, government approval, and changes in public opinion over time."},{"title":"Manifesto Project Main Dataset – Party Preferences (2020a)","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.25522/manifesto.mpds.2020a","justification":"A comparative dataset containing coded policy positions and political priorities derived from election manifestos. Includes German political parties and their programmes for elections during the 2010s, including the 2013 and 2017 federal elections. Useful for analysing party ideology, political competition, policy agendas, government formation, and changes in the German party system."},{"title":"German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES) – Candidate Campaign Survey 2013","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.12043","justification":"Dataset examining candidates participating in Germany's 2013 federal election, including representatives of major political parties such as CDU, CSU, SPD, FDP, Bündnis 90/Die Grünen, and Die Linke. Contains information relevant to political candidates, electoral campaigning, political organisations, and candidate characteristics. Especially suitable for research on political representation, party organisation, and electoral competition."},{"title":"German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES) – Candidate Studies 2009, 2013 and 2017","url_or_doi":"https://erato.wzb.eu/en/research/completed-research-programs/democracy-and-democratization/downloads","justification":"A collection of candidate-level election studies covering German federal elections, including those held in 2013 and 2017. Provides opportunities to investigate candidate characteristics, political recruitment, party affiliation, campaign activities, and political representation. Particularly relevant for studying German political parties and electoral organisations throughout the 2010s."},{"title":"German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES) – Pre- and Post-Election Surveys 2013 and 2017","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/gles/daten-und-dokumentation","justification":"Contains surveys administered before and after the German federal elections of 2013 and 2017. Relevant for investigating voter preferences, political attitudes, campaign effects, party evaluations, and electoral decision-making. The pre- and post-election design supports analysis of how political campaigns and media exposure relate to changes in political behaviour."},{"title":"German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES) – Long-Term Panels 2009–2013 and 2013–2017","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/gles/overview","justification":"Longitudinal survey datasets following respondents across multiple German federal elections. The panels covering 2009–2013 and 2013–2017 enable analysis of individual-level changes in political attitudes, voting behaviour, party identification, and political engagement. Particularly valuable for examining political stability and change during the 2010s."},{"title":"GESIS German Elections – Web and Social Media Data","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/elections/web-data","justification":"A research data collection focused on social media and web-based political communication surrounding German elections. Includes resources relating to the 2017 federal election and the 2019 European Parliament election campaign. Useful for studying digital political discourse, online campaigning, interactions between political organisations and citizens, and the role of social media platforms in electoral politics."},{"title":"ALLBUS Cumulative Dataset 1980–2018","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/allbus/data-and-documentation","justification":"A harmonised longitudinal collection of German General Social Survey data that includes survey waves throughout the 2010s. Supports research on changes in political trust, democratic attitudes, social values, political engagement, and broader societal developments. Its extended time coverage makes it especially useful for comparing German political attitudes during the 2010s with earlier decades."}]}
